action_summary: The guided repair could not repair a real third-party bug it was aimed at. Two causes, both measured on pluggy 3fc9e561 with the machine's own instrumented bug at src/pluggy/_manager.py:247. (1) EVIDENCE: the failing stack names the raise at :251; the faulty predicate is the guard at :247. The search's evidence rule was a +/-2-line window around the named line, so the only site that mattered scored 0 and 24 slots filled with unrelated constants. Graded proximity was not enough either: the true site scored 9600 and eight constants three lines from a different frame scored 9700. The rule that works is the one the language states -- a frame inside a branch body implicates that branch's own condition. (2) MODULE ROOT: _import_root_dirs walked parents only, so a src/ layout was invisible; the baseline then failed on an import, every candidate tied the baseline, and the search reported no repair exists. Measured: source_root=src -> 79 passed, rc 0; source_root=repo -> 2 failed, 77 passed -- a PYTHONPATH defect wearing the costume of a capability zero. With both fixed, apply_verified returns PASS__VERIFIED_REPAIR_APPLIED_AND_VERIFIED_IN_PLACE, applied=True, one file written, post-apply rc 0, in 18 s (was OPEN__NO_VERIFIED_REPAIR_IN_BOUNDED_SEARCH at 219 s). The front door still refuses the same task in four sentence shapes; that residue is recorded in execution_guard/MULTISTEP_DOOR_RECEIPTS_20261101.json and reported as unresolved.
